steps.title: Add lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Pour 1 mL of lysis buffer into the tube. The buffer contains 100 mmol Tris‑HCl (pH 8.0), 25 mmol EDTA (pH 8.0), 500 mmol NaCl, and 1 % SDS.

steps.title: Grind tissue to powder
steps.instruction: Using liquid nitrogen, grind approximately 200 mg of tissue into a fine powder.

steps.title: Thaw formaldehyde
steps.instruction: Thaw formaldehyde for 1 hour at room temperature before beginning the assay. (Wear gloves and safety glasses; work in a fume hood.)

steps.title: Combine powder with lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer the powdered tissue into a 2 mL tube that already contains the 1 mL lysis buffer. Note: for seawater samples, after 10 min on ice the sample is ready for slide preparation.

steps.title: Incubate lysate
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 56 °C in a water incubator for 30–180 minutes, mixing by inversion every 5–10 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate
steps.instruction: Allow the sample to cool to room temperature, then centrifuge at 16 700 × g for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous phase to a new 1.5 mL tube, add isopropyl alcohol equal to 2/3 of the supernatant volume, invert gently at least three times, and place the tube at –20 °C for 2 hours to precipitate DNA.

steps.title: Pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 16 700 × g for 10 minutes and carefully remove the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL TE buffer (Roche catalog #5618215001) to the DNA pellet and mix until fully dissolved.
